en: Laws of bran on Passover. Containing 3 seifim: One may not soak bran for chickens under any circumstances, nor may one scald it. {Rama: And when giving them barley or wheat to eat, one should be careful not to throw them in a wet place where they might become leavened. (Mahariv)}
A woman may not rub bran on her skin, even if it is dry.

If one rubbed bran on a goose wet from water, some say the goose is forbidden. {Rama: And this is the custom regarding the chametz prohibition, which applies even in the smallest amount. One should be careful not to singe fowl with straw, lest there be wheat or leavened grain there that imparts flavor to the fowl during singeing.}
In any case. Even if one does not intend to leave it the measure of mil, l'chatchila it is forbidden to leave it even a moment, as in siman 459 seif 2:

Nor scald. Because we are not expert in scalding as in siman 454 seif 3; Maharash of Kaidenburg responsum 27 wrote: one with stomach illness called hiben motir—remedy is scalding barley or oat sheaf placed on stomach; if this illness occurs on Passover with danger, a Jew may himself make chametz and heal; but if possible through a gentile he should; if impossible, boil water well then put barley so it does not leaven through scalding. If possible with fruit juice, do so for then it does not leaven—end. See siman 528 seif 13 and Taz there small seif 7:
Wet. Even before Passover one should be careful lest it leaven and remain there during Passover—see Knesset HaGedolah:
Dry. For we fear it will become moist afterward. It appears even if she does not rinse afterward in cold water they were stringent—Taz. See Chafetz Chayim:

In the smallest amount. We fear some chametz remains in goose crevices; even if skinning, whole goose forbidden—see Or Zarua. From six hours onward, since no stringency of smallest-amount prohibition, one may be lenient—Chafetz Chayim see there:

Flavor. B'dieved permitted—Taz (for it is fruit juice and they do not say perhaps water came on them, for they permitted siman 463 roasting two sheaves—even one forbidden; see Rashba and Chafetz Chayim). Magen Avraham wrote: only when unspecified; but if known there was leavened grain and they singed with it—forbidden; if singed with straw and later leavened grain found in remaining straw—we do not presume forbidden; but if three found—doubt, requires study (per Taz citing Rabbeinu Yerucham YD 84 that not so except worms that multiplied from it; see Magen Avraham 467 (7)(9); see Chafetz Chayim). Pri Megadim: if hollow oat stalk found without grain—see siman 454 s.k. 1:
Mishnah Pesachim 39
Tur in name of Geonim, as above
Mishnah there; Rosh wrote there that nowadays one should refrain; so Tur in his name
Tur in name of Avi HaEzri

461—in any case. Meaning not like Abaye who permits when not leaving mil measure—nevertheless l'chatchila forbidden as above siman 459 seif 2. Tur. And what he permitted regarding fowl pecking—is like dripping, nevertheless l'chatchila forbidden:
And not scald. Av HaGedolah and Magen Avraham:
And when giving them as explained—one may not soak, etc.:
463—if they rubbed. For it has crevices as Shabbos ch. 4 and we say chapter Kol HaBasar; if it has cracks forbidden:

And this is the custom, etc. Meaning even though in other prohibitions Shulchan Aruch YD 91 rules if cracks forbidden only in hot roasting; Beit Hillel wrote in cold roasting here follow poskim who forbid even live cold since smallest amount; and Magen Avraham; proof from Avodah Zarah 65b if cracked, etc.—grain is different, forbidden even cold:
One should be careful, etc., or leavened grain. Meaning water fell and it leavened—Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham:

In any case—see Mishna Berurah. Mechaber wrote thus to exclude Rambam's view; see Rambam ch. 5 chametz u'matzah three advices: feed immediately; or stand watching crop does not stand mil measure—second: as long as fowl eat and peck it does not leaven even if stands long; third: as long as he turns crop by hand it does not leaven—Itur objected forbidden to leave l'chatchila even less than mil; Ritva on Pesachim also objected pecking view. Gra wrote even dripping is only b'dieved. See Pri Chadash. Know on turning by hand while eating—Rambam's view—no explicit disputant; possibly all agree l'chatchila permitted like any dough where we hold while working it does not leaven; nevertheless requires study since Mechaber wrote one may not soak in any manner implies stringency here too:
In Magen Avraham s.k. 5 however Taz, etc., we do not say so. Note: see below siman 467 s.k. 12:
In any case. Even if not intending to leave mil measure, l'chatchila forbidden to leave even a moment as Mechaber above siman 459 seif 2—see there s.k. 6.

And not scald. Because we are not expert in scalding as above siman 454 seif 3 see there s.k. 4. Maharash Kaidenburg responsum 27: stomach illness hiben motir—scalding barley or oat sheaf on stomach; if on Passover with danger Jew may make chametz and heal; if possible through gentile; if impossible boil water well then barley without leavening through scalding; though we forbid scalding, whatever possible more permissibly we do; if possible with fruit juice—for then no leavening—end. See siman 528 seif 12 and Taz s.k. 7:
Or wheat to eat. Mahariv siman 193 wrote: those not eating chickens first days, last days eat—found no way unless careful during Passover feed only matzah not any grain—end. See siman 466 s.k. 47:
Wet place. Mahariv wrote even before Passover beware lest leaven and remain during Passover; see Knesset HaGedolah explaining courtyard youths; see above siman 433 s.k. 12:

Even dry. Tur wrote reason: must remove all bran before rinsing in water and nowadays women are not expert—end. Therefore if she transgressed and rubbed bran, do not rinse in cold afterward until known all passed, or rinse first in fruit juice:

And this is custom for chametz prohibition in smallest amount—meaning though Rosh forbids, his main proof from chapter 25 if cracks forbidden, and he extends to other prohibitions forbid whole if crevices as YD 91—but we rule like poskim there forbid whole only in roasted or boiled as Shulchan Aruch YD 91 seif 7 in gloss; nevertheless here for chametz smallest amount we are stringent like Rosh and forbid whole, for besides skin there are crevices in goose flesh on every side; so Darkei Moshe and Rav's son-in-law in Eshel Avraham unlike his error; see siman 467 s.k. 41—even those permitting cold agree here since cracks and rubbing causes entry—end. From six hours onward no smallest-amount stringency—lenient—it appears to me:

Not to singe. B'dieved if singed permitted—Taz; Magen Avraham: only unspecified; if known leavened grain and singed—forbidden b'dieved siman 92; if singed straw then leavened grain in remaining straw—we do not presume forbidden; if three found—doubt. If hollow oat stalk without grain—see siman 454 s.k. 1:

Seif 3 in gloss: beware not singe fowl with straw lest wheat or leavened grain—note see Taz and Magen Avraham even if grain found do not concern perhaps more were there. I was asked by Rav of Kraske: in practice hollow upper husk of oat sheaf found in water, checked no kernel—what law? I answered: per questioner's wording husk on strainer lid—if actual oat sheaf in crevice obviously permitted, for we do not presume prohibition place to place; can attribute to bucket drawing water to pour barrels briefly, not this pit water—no prohibition. Even per Maharam if husk in water also no prohibition as only doubt soaked; thus doubt perhaps no kernel; even if say perhaps not soaked long—still only rabbinic smallest doubt unlike Beit Lechem Yehudah bone marrow case d'oraisa doubt. Besides logic: even husk without kernel in food permitted—great rule we do not presume more evil than evident; certainly per Minchat Yaakov disputing Beit Lechem Yehudah hollow bone—forbidden only because common marrow in bone, custom marrow dissolves in pot, senses testify—if full marrow in food later comes out clean; here kernel in husk uncommon, not removed without hands, if falls occasionally kernel uncommon—not presumed especially rabbinic smallest amount—permitted without doubt; so I ruled several times permit even in food—requires study:
[1] And not scald, etc.—see siman 457 s.k. 5 for medical use permitted:

[2] Not to throw them, etc.—I do not see reason, for middle of courtyard needs no bedikah; perhaps Mahariv's law is courtyard youths (Knesset HaGedolah 433)—not so, Mahariv discusses middle; reason to forbid: certainly chametz requiring burning as above; even before Passover beware throwing in wet place lest remain during Passover:

[3] [Levush] when wanting to wash, etc.—implies when not wanting to wash permitted; in hints chapter Kol Sha'ah implies forbidden always—this is Taz's wording; appears even if not rinse afterward in cold they were stringent lest not rinse well—end his words; perforce scribal error requires study; seemed to emend: even if rinse, etc., meaning if before bathing rinses in cold that does not leaven as siman 457—then permitted afterward, for rinsing removed all; not that perhaps not rinse well; but Rosh and R' Yitzchak wrote must remove all bran before cold rinse:

Even dry—see EH s.k. 4 the reason. What in siman 450 permits heating hot water in chametz vessel to wash—for no benefit from absorbed vessel; here body benefits from prohibition. If rubbed, rinse in fruit juice or wait until certainly passed—Chafetz Chayim; also those not eating fowl first Passover days, last days ate—found no way unless careful feed only matzah all Passover days:

(1) [Seif 1] One may not soak bran, etc.—because it leavens in soaking—Rashi Pesachim 39b. Bran also leavens. R' Ovadiah siman 454 (1); Eliyah Rabbah (1); R' Zalman (3); Chafetz Chayim this siman (1); Mishna Berurah (2); see Shaar HaTziyun citing several great ones—see there. See our words there (3); bran and coarse bran explained there (2)—see there.
(2) There. One may not soak bran, etc.—from sixth hour onward. R' Zalman (1).

(3) There. In any case. Even if not leaving mil measure, l'chatchila forbidden even a moment as siman 459 seif 2 see there (1); Magen Avraham s.k. 1; Chafetz Chayim (1); Chok Yosef (1); Terumat Moshe (1); R' Zalman (1).
Taz s.k. 3 and it is in chapter Kol HaBasar if cracks, etc.—so it should read:
(s.k. 1) In any case even if not, etc.—meaning why wrote in any case to forbid even if not leaving—learn from this:
(s.k. 2) And not, etc.—siman 454 s.k. 3 regarding b'dieved if scalded:

(s.k. 3) Even, etc.—will become moist afterward—meaning though woman herself now moist at rubbing from sweat, nothing in that, for human sweat does not leaven as siman 466 seif 5; rather after rubbing custom to rinse in cold and we fear perhaps not remove all bran from body, some bran remains when rinsing cold and leavens; Taz's words here mistaken, require emendation:
In any case. Even if not leaving mil measure, l'chatchila forbidden even a moment as siman 459 seif 2:
And not scald. We are not expert in scalding—siman 454 s.k. 3:
Even dry. We fear it will become moist afterward:
That it is in smallest amount. We fear some chametz remains in goose crevices; unlike other prohibitions even with crevices do not forbid as YD 91 (Darkei Moshe)—see siman 467 s.k. 12:

Not to singe. B'dieved permitted (Taz); only unspecified; if known leavened grain and singed—forbidden b'dieved siman 92; above siman 446; if singed straw then leavened grain in remaining straw—we do not presume forbidden; if three found—doubt if comparable to worms YD 84 s.k. 9 presumed; however Taz wrote citing Rabbeinu Yerucham we do not say so except worms multiplying from it, not from outside—see there; here say at time all fell and only what we see remains; even if grain remained perhaps not leavened—see siman 467 s.k. 11:
(1) One may not soak, etc.—because they leaven like grain itself:
(2) Bran—and likewise coarse bran leavens. [Above siman 454 Mishna Berurah s.k. 2 explained bran and coarse bran.] Husk of straw holding grain called spreyer does not leaven, like ordinary straw:

(3) In any case—meaning not effective to stand watching so bran not in water mil measure—for that measure is only b'dieved; l'chatchila forbidden even one moment as above siman 459 seif 2—see Biur Halacha:

(4) And not scald—scalding means boil water very well then put flour or coarse bran; though scalding does not leaven, forbidden because we are not expert in scalding as above siman 454 seif 3—see Mishna Berurah there many details:

(5) Not to throw them, etc.—from sixth hour onward; some wrote even before Passover beware [unless standing over them while eating until finished and remainder not left before them] lest leaven and remain during Passover:
(6) Wet place—even if placed in dry place, good to beware not giving water to drink while barley before them; rather clean place well first then give water:

(7) Even dry—custom to enter bathhouse, sweat, rub body with bran—no concern since bran not soaked in water and body itself no water only bathhouse sweat, human sweat does not leaven; must remove all bran from all flesh before bathing in hot or cold water; since women nowadays not expert, prevent rubbing bran on flesh even dry. If transgressed, do not rinse cold afterward until known all passed or rinse first in fruit juice [Chafetz Chayim]:

(8) Wet goose—in Tur they soaked bran first in water; Mechaber ruled even dry bran only goose wet from water—novelty that even slight moisture on bird bran leavens and goose forbidden even if not rinsed afterward except fruit juice:
(9) Goose forbidden—because skin has many holes, bran remains; even if wants to rub and rinse afterward ineffective:

(10) And this is custom for chametz, etc.—meaning though for other prohibitions taste of holes ineffective to forbid unless meat hot or at least cooked or roasted and absorbed deep; here for chametz forbidden in smallest amount we concern even live if chametz remains in goose holes. Later authorities wrote even if wants to skin entirely—forbidden, bran enters through skin deep into flesh:

(11) That it is in smallest amount—since main reason is smallest-amount prohibition, from six hours until Passover nullified in sixty, may permit goose with good rubbing and rinsing in water provided eat before Passover lest something visible remains and revives on Passover; some lenient even eat during Passover where great loss:

(12) Not to singe, etc., wheat or leavened grain—meaning water fell after detachment and it leavened; later authorities agreed all this is mere l'chatchila caution; from basic law even if wheat there we do not presume leavened; even if known leavened, do not forbid since bird not touching grain holding it from above and flame rises below. If empty stalk found dissolved in food, do not concern perhaps leavened grain in stalk fell and dissolved:

Even—Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham emended: even rinse in cold means cold does not leaven; and R' Yehoshua (3) challenged Rosh clearly forbids rinsing afterward; see 467 and 413 even if not rinse cold afterward forbidden (human sweat does not leaven) decree lest not rinse well—for what. Know this bran in Mishnah disputed what it is—siman 454 Magen Avraham (1) if thick or thin husk, both in wheat not spreyer for sheaf certainly does not leaven. However also bran requires study, for I saw Rav Penei Yehoshua Pesachim 39b soaking bran is hardened chametz not fit for eating—see there; Mishna Berurah 447 (5) hardened nullified in sixty—say bran nullified in sixty—Peri Chadash; from Mishna Berurah gloss (3) bran in goose not smallest amount—say impossible without flour adhering as Magen Avraham 454 (1); see Tractate Terumot 1:5 distinction old/new—thus possible old without flour; in 454 we wrote from this much difference, also last Yom Tov day—see 467:

Goose forbidden—Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham and Peri Chadash; Mechaber YD 91 seif 7 permits cracks in cold roasting with rinsing; how much more live on Passover smallest amount—stringent as Mishna Berurah gloss; therefore wrote some forbid. Mechaber's way often writes some forbid not ruling dispute; or found only one authority; Avi HaEzri, Rosh, Tur forbid goose per their view YD Tur—even live with cracks forbids whole unlike Mechaber permits even cold roasted cracks, especially live; but stringency for chametz smallest amount. Cold roasting forbidden there Mishna Berurah without heter—here chametz perhaps b'dieved permitted by law during Passover. Question benefit from live cracks—sell to gentile like that case—perhaps forbidden by law—requires study. See 467 and (8) explained more:

And imparts flavor—Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham implies even if wheat found inside permitted, fruit juice though bird later cooked already nullified while still permitted before leavening. Not concerned wheat perhaps already leavened—we do not presume prohibition so certainly; responsa Tzemach Tzedek 122; above 462 wheat in honey permitted, not concerned already leavened. But leavened wheat and singed—implies forbid as Magen Avraham (5); but Eshel Avraham letter (4) permits even without husk since only chametz smell not touching—see there; in great need perhaps permit via husk anyway as 467 Magen Avraham (37) doubt like this. Perhaps difference singeing here smoke from chametz is like chametz as Magen Avraham (5)—see Taz 92 (8) sweat rises as 447 dry meat smoke from itself forbidden; Magen Avraham 451 for one view; therefore forbid whole bird if leavened wheat found unlike tar where fire extracts leaf to bird we do not say—see 467 Magen Avraham (37) Taz (21) and (8) explained. Peri Chadash 467 implies forbid when known leavened wheat—see there:
Magen Avraham s.k. 5 and singed with it—see below siman 467:

Scald, Beit Yosef—and see siman 528 in Taz meaning there writes not to do through gentile for illness without danger; Emunat Shmuel appears like Rama there if possible delay, do through gentile; nevertheless afterward if impossible appears boil, etc., implies also with danger; Ateret Shlomo wrote even though we forbid scalding, whatever possible permissibly we do as Mor U'Ketzia YD 255 end: do not permit any prohibition to sick if can heal permissibly like orlah though needs waiting for heter—clearly without danger discussed; rather with danger do not wait to boil if can do earlier since danger—some see error in wording but as written and means: first case without danger; from nevertheless whatever possible implies with danger, otherwise without gentile if not scalding truly forbidden like not chewing—practical law permit scalding for illness without danger too, for in 454 Magen Avraham doubts b'dieved forbid and Chafetz Chayim lenient to leave; no Beit Yosef concern; medical need certainly permitted not usual way as Ateret Shlomo; see below 466 s.k. 1; these Beit Yosef words from Leket Kemach imply danger case—for our view permit without danger too; see 466 s.k. 1:

Even dry. We fear some remains when she rinses in water; and do not say from end siman 450 permitting heating hot water in chametz vessel on Passover to wash—for there no benefit from vessel absorption; here chametz visible and woman benefits rubbing. Appears even if rinse afterward in cold they were stringent lest not rinse well:
Goose forbidden—because skin has cracks. In skin and gravy if cracks forbidden:

And imparts flavor to fowl. B'dieved do not forbid, for fruit juice and do not leaven; and do not say perhaps water once came on that straw—for then why permit 463 two sheaves—even one forbidden from this concern; rather certainly do not presume prohibition; Beit Yosef cites Rashba responsum 467 no concern leavening in sheaves; here not caution but l'chatchila extra stringency:
